claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 17 and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'd like to learn more about Alex's situation to assess your eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in sixth form, college, doing A-levels, or enrolled in any approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school but hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have a few more questions about Alex's situation:

**Is Alex currently working? If so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. 

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?** (If he has recently left education or training and registered with one of these, you may still be able to claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with anything like that. He just finished school and hasn't really sorted out his next steps yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

Since Alex is 17 years old (over 16), Child Benefit normally only continues if he stays in approved education or training. As Alex is not currently in any education or training program, this condition is not met.

There is a special provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks if a 16 or 17-year-old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. However, since Alex has not registered with either of these, this doesn't apply to your situation either.

**What could change this?**

If Alex were to:
- Enroll in approved education or training (such as college, sixth form, or an approved training program), or
- Register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services

Then you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit for him. If his circumstances change, you would be able to make a claim at that point.

I hope this clarifies your situation. If you have any other questions, please feel free to ask.
